# chaoss-community-activity Specification

<!-- Generated by Prism from prism/spec.json. Change the app through your agent with /prism, not by editing this file. -->

## Purpose

Community Activity indicator: The ISO/IEC 15939 indicator of the CHAOSS metrics model Community Activity: from how many of its 11 measures have an admitted observation and how many were refused, tell whether its information need is answered, partly answered, unmeasured or an open claim.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Never complete when refused is at least 1

The app SHALL NOT answer `complete` when refused is at least 1, because an information need with a refused base measure is never answered complete.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-001, theorem `inv001Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-001 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `1 1` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `complete`
- **AND** the app answers `open`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: Never complete when admitted is below 11

The app SHALL NOT answer `complete` when admitted is below 11, because an information need is answered complete only when every base measure is admitted.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-002, theorem `inv002Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-002 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `10 0` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `complete`
- **AND** the app answers `partial`, decided by the fallback

### Requirement: Always complete when refused equals 0 and admitted is at least 11

The app SHALL answer `complete` when refused equals 0 and admitted is at least 11, because every base measure admitted and none refused answers the information need.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-003, theorem `inv003Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-003 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `11 0` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `complete`
- **AND** the app answers `complete`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: Never unmeasured when admitted is at least 1 and refused equals 0

The app SHALL NOT answer `unmeasured` when admitted is at least 1 and refused equals 0, because an admitted base measure is never reported unmeasured.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-004, theorem `inv004Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-004 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `11 0` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `unmeasured`
- **AND** the app answers `complete`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: REQ-001 open when refused is at least 1

The app SHALL answer `open` when refused is at least 1, because AGENTS.md R2: a refused observation is measured and reported, never restated as an answer; CC-03 carries an unmatched member the same way.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule1`).

#### Scenario: REQ-001 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `1 1` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `open`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: REQ-002 complete when admitted is at least 11

The app SHALL answer `complete` when admitted is at least 11 and no earlier rule matches, because ISO/IEC 15939 indicator: every base measure of wg-metrics-models@4365fe61cf9654ef7b3911805425f4e485918672:metrics-model-libs/community-activity/definition/community-activity.md (sha256:505814967c8e390e88df1206e774b421b7b259f3f11554862d69324.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule2`).

#### Scenario: REQ-002 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `11 0` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `complete`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: REQ-003 unmeasured when admitted equals 0

The app SHALL answer `unmeasured` when admitted equals 0 and no earlier rule matches, because ISO/IEC 15939: an indicator with no base measure measured answers no information need.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule3`).

#### Scenario: REQ-003 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `0 0` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `unmeasured`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: Otherwise partial

The app SHALL answer `partial` when no rule matches, because some base measures are admitted, none refused and some not yet observed.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: No rule matches

- **WHEN** the request is `10 0` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `partial`

### Requirement: The first matching rule decides

The app SHALL try REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003 in that order, and the first rule that matches SHALL decide.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: Two rules match

- **WHEN** the request is `0 1`
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `open`, decided by REQ-001, the earlier rule

### Requirement: Request and answers

The app SHALL read one request as one line of 2 fields separated by single spaces, in this order, and SHALL answer exactly one of `open`, `complete`, `unmeasured`, `partial`, or `invalid` for anything else.

| Field | Accepts | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `admitted` | whole number from 0 up to 11 | how many of the model's 11 measures have an observation uor-observation-admission permitted: Contributor Count; Updated Issues Count; Recent Releases Count; Updated Since; Code Review Count; Organization Count; Commit Frequency; Issue Comme |
| `refused` | whole number from 0 up to 11 | how many of them had their observation refused |

| Answer | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `open` | a base measure was refused, so the information need stays an open claim |
| `complete` | every one of the 11 measures has an admitted observation, so the information need is answered |
| `unmeasured` | no base measure has an admitted observation yet |
| `partial` | some base measures have admitted observations and none was refused |
| `invalid` | the request is malformed |

Verified: reading a request is tested, not proved.

#### Scenario: A malformed request is invalid

- **WHEN** the request is not 2 fields in this order
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `invalid`

## Examples

- `11 0` gives `complete`
- `10 0` gives `partial`
- `0 0` gives `unmeasured`
- `1 1` gives `open`

## What is proved and what is tested

Lean proves each property marked proved above, for every request that decodes, with no exceptions and no sampling. The proof is about `judge`, the function the WebAssembly guest runs, because both come from the same model.

The parsing of requests is tested, not proved: the acceptance vectors in the app replay through the built guest, including malformed and oversized requests.

Nothing here says the rules are the right rules. That is the part only you can judge.
